column1: # Every persisted derived body, versioned by its compaction code rather than
# the release. Columns: representation name, version, comma-separated source
# files whose text produces the derived bytes (the owning crate's file
# first), comma-separated Cargo.lock packages whose locked versions the
# derive's bytes depend on (`-` when none), and the sha256 of the sources
# The version lives at the `Derived::new` or `representation` call site; the
# parity test in the owning crate (derive_parity.rs) checks this table and
# that every `Derived::new("<name>"` in the crate's sources is registered.
# When a transform's source changes, the test fails naming the new hash:
# bump the version and update this row in the same commit. A row must list
# every file the derive reads bytes through; whole files are hashed, so a
# formatting or comment edit in a listed file also needs the bump (batch
# cosmetic edits in these files). `crates/http/src/derive.rs` is in every
# transform's set because it feeds and parses the body.
# The listed packages are not hashed here. The cache's build script
# fingerprints their locked versions into the representation
# (`name@vN~<fingerprint>`), so a dependency bump misses exactly the bodies
# whose row lists it, with no version bump. The parity test only checks
# that every listed package is in Cargo.lock, so a typo fails.
